source_lines: maya: someone at my internship microwaved curry at 10am and i have been suffering ever since
liam: curry. yes. i'm in before you even ask

constraints_found.constraint: Preference: fast lunch, no long sit-down (Maya must be back by 1:00)
source_lines: maya: also my manager does a head count at 1:00 sharp. i cannot be the one strolling back in at 1:20
liam: so no long sit-down lunch. in, eat, out. my stomach and i are ready
maya: and the trip fund is watching. if it's pricey, i'm eating crackers at my desk
maya: badly. my iced tea this morning cost what a whole lunch should. downtown is robbing me

constraints_found.constraint: Strict diet: Mina is vegetarian (implied; needs real meat-free mains, several curry options)
source_lines: liam: ok ok. but mina orders a real main this time. no plate of fries
liam: burger day in spring. i had a double stack. she had fries, because nothing else on the menu worked for her
maya: oh, like pizza day when she offered to pick the pepperoni off. absolutely not
mina: ...okay. somewhere with a few curries i can actually order would be really nice. thank you both

elimination.downtown_copper_pot: Deal-breaker: all curries are lamb, chicken or beef; vegetarian only gets plain rice.
elimination.downtown_cardamom_house: $$ is one tier over budget (-1 star); otherwise fits. 2 stars.
elimination.downtown_indigo_arch: Slow coursed sit-down service, reviewer was late back to the office (missed speed preference, -1 star). 2 stars.
elimination.downtown_pepper_tree: Burgers, misses the curry craving (-1 star); veg patty and fast are fine. 2 stars.
elimination.downtown_tamarind_lane: Curry, $, counter service with time to spare, three vegetarian curries. 3 stars.

notes: The vegetarian diet is never stated outright; it is implied through the burger-day fries and pepperoni-picking callbacks plus Mina's 'a few curries i can actually order'. Fair and satisfying, but a player who skims the banter could miss it and pick Copper Pot.
The burger-day callback might also tempt a careless player toward Pepper Tree, but the review language ('doesn't eat meat') makes the veg reading clear.
Budget is implied rather than stated as a tier; 'if it's pricey' plus the iced tea complaint reads as $. Treating $$ as one over is my assumption.
Every venue review uses the same 'coworker/friend who doesn't eat meat' phrasing, which makes the veg constraint a bit easy to confirm once you suspect it.
The night-market noodle stall line is a red herring/setup; no venue matches it and Maya explicitly dismisses it. Fine.
